editorial.headline: Other Hospital Services: Nationally Open, Address-Sensitive in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This hospital-services activity is open to full foreign ownership nationally and is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium, though the proposed address still requires verification.
editorial.body:
### A residual hospital-services category

This activity sits within hospital services as the category for other health-care and physical-treatment work not included in the specifically enumerated hospital activities. That restrained wording matters. It is not a broad label for every venture with a clinical dimension; its centre of gravity remains hospital activity. The classification provides room for the remaining health-care and physical-treatment activity described by its scope, so the real question is whether the proposed care or treatment belongs within that hospital-services setting.

On scale, the record gives one clear answer: **Besar**. It is the only scale open to this activity. That makes the registration profile unusually focused: the classification is available to operators registering at the large scale stated in the record, rather than across a range of business scales. Nothing in the record adds a separate applicant type, licence pathway, capital threshold, or timetable, so those should not be inferred from the activity title alone.

For foreign investment at the national level, the position is direct. The activity is marked **TERBUKA**, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In practical terms, the national classification permits full foreign ownership. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. There is no lesser foreign-share ceiling recorded here, and no partnership condition is attached to the national PMA position in this slim record.

Bali calls for a closer reading, without warranting pessimism. The Bali status is recorded as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, with the activity described as medium-high/high risk and therefore not blocked by the provincial moratorium. That moratorium blocks low and medium-low risk KBLI activities for PMA across the province; this activity is outside that blocked category on the record presented. The important qualification is geographical rather than numerical: the record says to verify the position for the proposed address. The honest conclusion is that a foreign investor is not shut out of Bali by this moratorium, while the address-specific check remains part of a careful registration assessment.
